title: Retry-After parsing (delta-seconds + HTTP-date) + jittered exponential backoff
author: Dana Lo
description: Context: As part of the cross-language SDK parity initiative (retry/timeout standard), TS currently only parses Retry-After when it is a delta-seconds value. The gateway and some upstreams also emit Retry-After as an HTTP-date (e.g. "Wed, 21 Oct 2015 07:28:00 GMT"), which we should respect to avoid retrying too aggressively during throttling. In addition, our retry middleware used a deterministic exponential backoff sequence, which can create synchronized retries (thundering herd) across many clients. This PR adds: (1) Retry-After parsing for both delta-seconds and HTTP-date formats, (2) jittered exponential backoff consistent with the parity standard, and (3) tests/fixtures to lock behavior. Behavior details: Retry-After parsing: If header is delta-seconds => wait = clamp(deltaSeconds*1000, 0..maxRetryAfterMs). If header is HTTP-date => wait = clamp(dateMs - nowMs, 0..maxRetryAfterMs). If parsing fails or results in NaN/negative => treat as absent and fall back to exponential backoff. We only honor Retry-After on status codes where we retry (429, 500/502/503/504), with primary focus on 429. Backoff + jitter: Introduce a jittered exponential backoff helper (baseDelayMs=250, multiplier=2, maxDelayMs=10_000) using full jitter: delay = randomInt(0..cap) where cap = min(maxDelayMs, baseDelayMs * 2^(attempt-1)). This matches the parity guidance and reduces retry synchronization under load. Backwards compatibility: No API surface changes; retry defaults remain the same maxAttempts. Only changes are (a) respecting additional valid Retry-After values and (b) adding jitter to the sleep, which may slightly change exact retry timing but improves reliability at scale. Testing: Adds unit tests for Retry-After parsing (seconds, HTTP-date, invalid, negative/0, far-future clamp) and for backoff jitter bounds. Also adds an integration-style test against the retry middleware with a simulated 429 + Retry-After HTTP-date to validate we wait at least the computed duration (with deterministic clock + stubbed RNG). Notes: This does not change streaming retry behavior (still conservative) and does not add any telemetry fields; those are tracked separately under ENG-5129.

conversation: Allison Grant (review): Can we confirm we handle both Retry-After formats (delta-seconds + HTTP-date) and clamp to a reasonable maximum? We should avoid sleeping for hours if the server sends a bad date.
Dana Lo (author): Yep. maxRetryAfterMs default is 60_000 (same as other SDKs). For HTTP-date we compute date-now and clamp to [0, maxRetryAfterMs]. Invalid parses fall back to normal backoff.
Ibrahim Khan (review): Please ensure negative/zero values don’t end up as a large unsigned delay somewhere. Also, can you avoid depending on Date parsing quirks across runtimes?

Dana Lo (author): Added explicit checks for NaN and <0. For HTTP-date we use Date.parse which is what node/fetch environments support; if parse fails we treat as absent. Also added a test covering invalid strings and negative computed delays.
Sean Gallagher (review): +1 on jitter. Which jitter algorithm did we settle on in the standard? Full jitter vs equal jitter vs decorrelated?

Dana Lo (author): Implemented full jitter (random 0..cap). That’s what we’ve been recommending in the parity standard to reduce synchronization. Added tests to ensure bounds and cap behavior are correct.
Allison Grant (review): Requesting change: honor Retry-After only on retryable codes; don’t accidentally sleep on 400s if someone toggles retryable status codes in the future.
Dana Lo (author): Updated middleware to only consult Retry-After after classification says retryable. Added a regression test that a 400 with Retry-After does not wait/retry.
Ibrahim Khan (review): Looks good. One minor: the integration test stubs Math.random globally; can we scope it to the helper?
Dana Lo (author): Adjusted helper to accept an optional rng() in test-only path and removed the global stub. CI now green.
release_notes: TypeScript SDK now respects Retry-After headers provided as HTTP-date in addition to delta-seconds, and retry backoff now uses jittered exponential delays to reduce synchronized retry storms. No public API changes.
